topic: Neck pain when driving: mirrors, headrest and breaks

slides.headline: Neck stiff after every road trip?
slides.sub: Your mirrors, headrest and breaks matter more than you might think.

slides.title: Set your seat first
slides.body: Sit with hips back in the seat and the backrest slightly reclined. Your hands should rest on the wheel with elbows gently bent, so your shoulders aren't reaching.

slides.title: Mirrors as a posture cue
slides.body: Adjust your mirrors while sitting tall. If you start slumping, the mirrors will look off. That's a useful reminder to sit back up, rather than readjusting them.

slides.title: Bring the headrest up
slides.body: The middle of the headrest should sit roughly level with the back of your head, and close to it. It's there to protect your neck, and it gives you something to rest back against.

slides.title: Break every two hours
slides.body: Stop, get out and walk for a few minutes. Look over each shoulder, roll your shoulders and do a few chin tucks. Share the driving where you can.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: Pain spreading down an arm, pins and needles or weakness in the hand, headaches that keep building, or neck pain after a car accident are worth an assessment.

caption:
Neck stiff and sore after every long drive?

Summer road trips mean hours in one position with your eyes locked on the road. Your neck can handle a lot, but it doesn't love staying still that long.

A few setup tweaks help: seat back and slightly reclined, mirrors set while you're sitting tall, and the headrest up level with the back of your head. Then stop every two hours to walk, look over each shoulder and roll your shoulders. Arm pain, pins and needles or pain after a crash are worth getting assessed.

story.headline: Long drive ahead?
story.body: Set mirrors sitting tall, raise the headrest level with your head, and stop every two hours to move.
